summary: Phase 149O.19.5G -- HMIC Assembled Attack Matrix / Hardening: ASSEMBLED ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION / HARDENING (Wave G) of the now-wired Wave A-F implementation (parser/model -> identity -> protected store -> validator -> admin -> readiness -> lock-held activation), gated as a verify-first phase with no new capability by default. Read docs/contracts/HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_CONTRACT.md (HMIC-001 v1.1) in full, plus src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py (2096 lines), src/pcae/core/hatp_mandatory_cutover.py (1025 lines), and scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py (537 lines) all in full, before writing any test. Independently reconstructed (not copied from prior phase reports) the 9-member CertificationStatus vocabulary, the 24-file HMIC v1.1 frozen scope (including all three self-referential production modules), and the 7-check readiness model (6 HMRC-REQ-054 items plus 1 module-owned repository_deployment_identity_valid check), matching every prior phase's claim. Added tests/test_phase_149o_19_5g_hmic_assembled_attack_matrix_hardening.py (68 tests, all passed), composing multiple layers per test rather than duplicating existing per-layer unit tests, covering: parser/model attacks; parsed-but-not-valid certifications; 24-file identity attacks including self-binding on all three frozen production modules; no-implicit-latest; active-invalid-not-superseded; validator status precedence under multi-defect certifications (matching HMIC-REQ-103's exact 12-step order); freshness/no-cache/read-only; authority-input-injection resistance; admin/agent-unreachability; the Wave F readiness re-attack; TOCTOU races against the lock-held activation recheck (revocation, binding change, implementation drift); one-way-cutover preservation; historical/pre-Wave-F replay rejection; and a no-fallback-chains search. Zero BLOCKING findings. Zero production or contract files changed -- confirmed all eight bound contracts (HMIC-001 v1.1, HMRC-001, HATP-001, HSCE-001, RAE-001, RWMPC-001, PBPA-001, PBPC-001) byte-unchanged at exit. Fast Green (pytest -m fast_green -n auto): 6253 passed, 24 failed (all pre-existing, A/B-confirmed), 2 skipped, 1 collection error (fido2 optional dependency not installed in this environment, pre-existing/unrelated). Verdict: HMIC ASSEMBLED WAVE A-F ATTACK MATRIX / HARDENING: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- ASSEMBLED CERTIFICATION -> READINESS -> ACTIVATION BOUNDARY HOLDS. No untrusted/caller/repository/environment-controlled input was found able to reach HMIC VALID, mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified=True, overall activation readiness=True, or a HATP_MANDATORY transition without satisfying every frozen prerequisite. One new non-blocking textual finding (F-149O.19.5G-1): certification_status_satisfies_readiness's own docstring still states it is 'never wired into hatp_mandatory_cutover.py by this phase (Wave F only, gated by Stop Condition W-1)' -- stale since 149O.19.5F actually performed that wiring; descriptive text only, no authority effect, not repaired this phase per the non-opportunistic-repair policy, flagged for a future documentation-only phase. W-1 remains independently closed only at the contract + implementation-identity boundary (deployment/runtime-source provenance still deferred). B-149O-1..4 remain closed only at the system implementation/enforcement boundary. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. validation_results.name: parser_model_attacks
validation_results.result: Malformed/unknown-field/wrong-type/unsafe-identifier/path-traversal-shaped/duplicate-key/NaN-Infinity artifacts are rejected at parse time or map to MALFORMED; no malformed artifact becomes a valid authority object.

validation_results.name: parsed_not_valid
validation_results.result: Well-formed but revoked/wrong-repo/wrong-deployment/wrong-implementation/wrong-contracts certifications never reach VALID; each maps to its exact contract-specified status via the real admin ceremony.

validation_results.name: identity_self_binding_attacks
validation_results.result: Omitting, adding, or modifying a frozen file -- including self-binding attacks on hatp_mandatory_certification.py, scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py, and hatp_mandatory_cutover.py -- changes the implementation-scope digest and invalidates any existing certification; unaffected by extra non-frozen files.

validation_results.name: no_implicit_latest_and_active_invalid_not_superseded
validation_results.result: Unbound certifications are never consulted (no sorted/glob/max/timestamp-based selection); an actively-bound revoked certification stays REVOKED even with a newer unbound valid-looking record present.

validation_results.name: validator_status_precedence_multi_defect
validation_results.result: Multi-defect certifications (revoked+implementation-mismatch, wrong-repo+revoked, implementation-mismatch+contract-mismatch, missing+everything) resolve to the exact status HMIC-REQ-103's 12-step algorithm dictates, not merely non-VALID.

validation_results.name: freshness_no_cache_read_only_authority_input
validation_results.result: No memoization decorator anywhere in the certification module; byte-identical protected root before/after repeated validation calls; the production validator entrypoint signature is exactly (repository_root) with no caller-suppliable repo/digest/valid=True-shaped parameter on any public or internal-seam signature; environment-variable injection has no effect.

validation_results.name: admin_agent_unreachability
validation_results.result: No src/pcae/** file besides the certification module itself references the admin writer primitives; no CLI/agent code path imports the admin script; ordinary agents/CLI have zero path to creating or revoking certification authority.

validation_results.name: readiness_reattack
validation_results.result: HMIC VALID alone with one other of the 6 HMRC-REQ-054 terms false still yields overall ready=False; HMIC non-VALID with all others true still yields overall ready=False; exact 9-member CertificationStatus-to-Boolean mapping confirmed, including a validator exception mapping False.

validation_results.name: toctou_lock_held_recheck
validation_results.result: Revocation, active-binding change, and implementation drift occurring between an advisory pre-lock read and the lock-held activation recheck each correctly refuse activation; Cutover Record byte-identical before/after; no activation marker written.

validation_results.name: one_way_cutover_preserved
validation_results.result: Post-activation revocation degrades readiness honestly but never reverses the Cutover Record's mode away from HATP_MANDATORY; no reverse transition-graph edge exists.

validation_results.name: historical_replay_rejected
validation_results.result: A v1.0/22-file-shaped digest never equals the full 24-file digest; the real pre-Wave-F vs post-Wave-F bytes of hatp_mandatory_cutover.py (a frozen member) produce different digest components, so a certification predating the Wave F edit cannot validate against current source.
